title: Sore Throat
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute sore throat, fever >38°C, tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and NO cough. Centor criteria score ≥3: rapid strep test or throat culture indicated. GAS pharyngitis is most common in children 5-15 years. Treatment: penicillin VK PO x 10 days or amoxicillin (first-line). Single-dose IM benzathine penicillin if adherence concern. Cephalexin or clindamycin if penicillin-allergic. Abx shorten symptoms by 1-2 days and prevent complications: acute rheumatic fever (most important), peritonsillar abscess, and PSGN (though Abx don't prevent PSGN). Patient can return to school 24h after starting antibiotics. Symptomatic: acetaminophen or NSAIDs, fluids. NO aspirin in children (Reye's).
chief_complaint: Acute sore throat, fever, tonsillar exudates, no cough
